data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure than a redundant monolith because it replaces homogeneous redundancy with operational heterogeneity, preventing 'single-binary' systemic collapses.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The services share a critical upstream dependency (e.g., a single cloud provider's identity service).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'independence' is purely organizational but the technical stack is converged (shadow monolith).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Heterogeneity acts as a biological-style firewall; diverse implementations of the same functional requirement (different OS, languages, or logic paths) ensure that a specific trigger (e.g., a kernel bug or a leap-second error) cannot achieve 100% penetration across the network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
